proof_points.claim: DiDi already owns the urban first/last mile in Latin America's coastal metros.
proof_points.evidence: DiDi is the market leader in Mexico — its largest market outside China — and owns Brazil's #1 ride-hail app, 99, with leading positions across Colombia, Costa Rica, Panama and the Dominican Republic. The demand layer beside these cruising grounds is already DiDi's.

proof_points.claim: The vessel is commercial today, not a concept.
proof_points.evidence: The N30 Pioneer II is in commercial service now — 70 nm range, ~30 kt — already operating with the Four Seasons on Lake Austin. This is a delivery-ready platform, not a 2030 promise.

proof_points.claim: A network at LatAm scale is already being built elsewhere.
proof_points.evidence: Navier is ramping a roughly 100-vessel water network in the Maldives with JIH Global over three years, and signed a national-scale agreement with WorldBridge in Cambodia in May 2026 — proof the model scales beyond single boats.

proof_points.claim: Foiling economics fit a price-sensitive, high-frequency mobility app.
proof_points.evidence: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water for dramatically lower energy per passenger-mile, with hybrid Quanta-LR range that needs no charging infrastructure — the cost structure a mobility network, not just a luxury charter, can run.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for Latin America's distances?
objections.response: Most island and bay crossings here are short — Cancún↔Isla Mujeres ~8 nm, Cartagena↔Rosarios ~17 nm, Vallarta↔Marietas ~20 nm — well inside the Pioneer II all-electric envelope. For the longer coastal legs (Rio↔Angra, Cabo↔La Paz) the Quanta-LR hybrid covers up to 700 nm with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: Our riders are price-sensitive — is this only for tourists?
objections.response: Tourism corridors fund the launch because the willingness-to-pay is highest there, but the same vessels run everyday water-commute and airport-gateway legs. Foiling's energy efficiency is precisely what lets a water tier sit inside a mass-market app rather than only a charter brand.

objections.concern: Why does a ride-hail app need boats it doesn't operate?
objections.response: You don't operate them. Navier brings the fleet, captains and maintenance; you bring demand, dispatch, the wallet and the brand — the same split that already works for cars, applied to the one transport surface in Latin America no one has digitized.

objections.concern: Is the regulatory path realistic across so many countries?
objections.response: We start market-by-market on existing berths and ferry corridors — no new infrastructure, no new rights-of-way. Each coastal cluster is a self-contained pilot; Cancún or Cartagena can prove the model before it scales region-wide.

end_state.headline: The water layer of Latin America's dominant ride-hail network.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every coastal metro DiDi and 99 already serve where islands, reefs or ferry corridors sit just offshore — Rio and the Costa Verde, Cancún and the Riviera Maya, Los Cabos and Vallarta, Cartagena, San Blas, Papagayo and Samaná.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II capillaries + Quanta-LR coastal legs
steady_state.tam_framing: Tens of millions of premium island and bay crossings a year, today served by slow ferries and unbookable pangas, moved into the DiDi app.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is not a pilot count — it is the coastal map of DiDi's footprint. Start where willingness-to-pay is highest (Cancún, Cartagena, Vallarta), prove the in-app water tier, then extend cluster by cluster until every DiDi coast has a clean, bookable water layer.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR), captain training, maintenance and the network operating system.
the_ask.partner_brings: Demand and dispatch through the DiDi/99 app, the wallet, the brand, and the choice of launch market.
the_ask.next_step: Scope a first pilot in one flagship cluster — Cancún or Cartagena — co-defining the in-app water tier on three corridors, with a path to region-wide rollout.

close.title: One app. Every DiDi coast. A water layer no one else owns yet.
close.body: DiDi already owns the demand beside Latin America's best cruising grounds. Water is the one surface still served by slow ferries and cash-only boatmen. Start in a single bay, prove the in-app foiling tier, and scale it across the coast DiDi already commands.
